- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s fading or reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot in 10-15 day horizon; apply smoothing or lag correction.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward moves; add a downward bias if recent 7-14 day average is above 3σ of historical volatility.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 1.00), model tends to misalign with sentiment shifts; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3-5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to anticipate further decline; add 1-2% downward bias unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias to reflect potential sentiment recovery or policy-driven support.
